key_insight: A multimodal cardiac foundation model pretrained on signals and textual reports from 1.7 million individuals enables consistent, interpretable cardiac health assessment across hospital and consumer devices. It generalizes across device types and settings, bridging clinical and at‑home monitoring.
problem_solved: Heterogeneity of heart signal sources (hospital ECGs vs. wearable/phone sensors), limited labeled clinical data, and lack of a unified model that provides reliable, interpretable cardiac assessments across devices and care settings.
method: Large‑scale multimodal pretraining on 1.7M individuals’ heart signals paired with clinician text/interpretations to learn shared representations.
Design for device‑agnostic transfer: apply the pretrained foundation model to hospital ECGs and a range of home/wearable sensors with minimal fine‑tuning or zero‑shot adaptation.
Produce clinically meaningful, interpretable outputs suitable for downstream tasks (diagnosis, triage, longitudinal monitoring) while maintaining robustness across settings.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to build scalable, generalizable cardiac applications that require less labeled data and transfer reliably between clinical and consumer devices—accelerating deployment of trustworthy digital cardiac health tools.

paper_title: Cardiac health assessment across scenarios and devices using a multimodal foundation model pretrained on data from 1.7 million individuals
paper_authors: Xiao Gu, Wei Tang, Jinpei Han, Veer Sangha, Fenglin Liu
